Recall that $\mathbb{L}^\ell$ and $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ are defined above. We can write $\mathbb{L}^\ell = \mathbb{B}_1^\ell \mathcal{P}_\infty^\ell \mathbb{V}_\infty$ and $\mathbb{R}^\ell = \mathbb{B}_2^\ell \mathcal{Q}_\infty^\ell \mathbb{V}_\infty$, where $\mathbb{B}_1^\ell = \mathrm{blkdiag}(B_{11}^\ell,\ldots,B_{1T}^\ell)$, $\mathbb{B}_2^\ell = \mathrm{blkdiag}(B_{21}^\ell,\ldots,B_{2T}^\ell)$ are $n\times(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}N_t)$ matrices,
$\mathbb{V}_{\infty}\equiv
(V_T',V_{T-1}',\ldots,V_1'$, $V_0',V_{-1}',\ldots)'$ is infinity dimensional vector,
$$\mathcal{P}_\infty^\ell = \begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{0}_{N_0 \times N_T} & \mathbf{0}_{N_0 \times N_{T-1}} & \dots & \mathbf{0}_{N_0 \times N_1} & B_{10}P_0^{(0)} & B_{10}P_0^{(1)} &  \dots \\
\mathbf{0}_{N_1 \times N_T} & \mathbf{0}_{N_1 \times N_{T-1}} & \dots & B_{11}P_1^{(0)} & B_{11}P_1^{(1)} & B_{11}P_1^{(2)} &  \dots \\
\vdots & \vdots & \iddots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots &  \ddots \\
\mathbf{0}_{N_{T-1} \times N_T} & B_{1,T-1}P_{T-1}^{(0)} & \dots & B_{1,T-1}P_{T-1}^{(T-2)} & B_{1,T-1}P_{T-1}^{(T-1)} & B_{1,T-1}P_{T-1}^{(T)} &  \dots
\end{pmatrix},$$ is $(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}N_t)\times\infty$ matrix, and $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^\ell$ is defined analogously.
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:Pinfty-UB}
Under Assumption~\ref{asp_A2}, both $\mathcal{P}_{\infty}^\ell$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^\ell$ are UB. Consequently,
$\mathbb{B}_1^\ell \mathcal{P}_\infty^\ell$ and $\mathbb{B}_2^\ell \mathcal{Q}_\infty^\ell$ are also UB.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We only prove the claim for $\mathcal{P}_{\infty}^\ell$, since the proof for $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^\ell$ is identical.
By Assumption~\ref{asp_A2} and Lemma \ref{lm33},
\[
\sup_{N,T}\|\mathcal{P}_{\infty}^\ell\|_{\infty}
\leq
\sup_{N,T}\sup_{0\le t\le T-1}
\left\|
\sum_{h=0}^{\infty}\mathrm{abs}\!\left(B_{1t}P_t^{(h)}D_{t-h}\right)
\right\|_{\infty}
<\infty,
\]
and
\[
\sup_{N,T}\|\mathcal{P}_{\infty}^\ell\|_{1}
\leq
\sup_{N,T}\sup_{t\le T-1}
\left\|
\sum_{h=t}^{\infty}\mathrm{abs}\!\left(D_h'B_{1h}P_h^{(h-t)}\right)
\right\|_{1}
<\infty.
\]
Hence $\mathcal{P}_{\infty}^\ell$ is UB. Since $\mathbb{B}_1^\ell$ is UB by Assumption~\ref{asp_A2},
$\mathbb{B}_1^\ell\mathcal{P}_{\infty}^\ell$ is also UB. The proof for
$\mathbb{B}_2^\ell\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^\ell$ is the same.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:infinite-qf-homo}
Suppose Assumption~2 holds. Let $\Pi_n$ be an $n\times n$ nonstochastic matrix that is UB, and let $\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}$ and $\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}$ be two nonstochastic $n\times\infty$ matrices that are UB. Define $\mathbb{M}_n\equiv \mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}$. Then
\begin{align}
E\!\left[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\Pi_n
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\right]
=
\sigma_0^2\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n),\label{eq_Einfty}    
\end{align}
and
\[
\mathrm{Var}\!\left[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\Pi_n
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\right]
=
(\mu_4-3\sigma_0^4)\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jj}^2
+
\sigma_0^4\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n')
+
\sigma_0^4\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n^2).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We have
\[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\Pi_n
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
=
\mathbb{V}_{\infty}'\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{V}_{\infty}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_j
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_k .
\]

Since $\Pi_n$, $\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}$ and $\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}$ are UB, the $n\times n$ matrix $\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'$ is UB, and hence
$\mathrm{tr}\!\left(
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\right)=O(n)$.
Similarly, the $n\times n$ matrices
$\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}'\Pi_n'\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'$
and
$\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'$
are also UB, and thus their traces are $O(n)$.
Therefore, we have
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\bigl|(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}\bigr|^2
=
\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n')
=
\mathrm{tr}\!\left(
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}'\Pi_n'
\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\right)<\infty.
\]
where the cyclic permutation of factors is legitimate because the matrix $\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}'\Pi_n'\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
$ is
$n\times n$ and hence finite-dimensional.
Additionally,
$\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}
\bigl|(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jj}\bigr|^2<\infty,$ and
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\bigl|(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}(\mathbb{M}_n)_{kj}\bigr|
\le
\frac12
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\left[
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}^2+(\mathbb{M}_n)_{kj}^2
\right]
=
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}^2
=
\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n')
<\infty.
\]

Hence the relevant series are absolutely summable. In particular, Tonelli's theorem is used in the
following two steps. First, for the expectation,
\[
E\!\left[
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_j
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_k
\right]
=
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}
E\!\left[
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_j
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_k
\right].
\]
Since the elements of $\mathbb{V}_{\infty}$ are i.i.d. with mean zero and variance $\sigma_0^2$,
only the terms with $j=k$ survive, so
\[
E\!\left[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\Pi_n
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\right]
=
\sigma_0^2
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jj}
=
\sigma_0^2\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n).
\]

Second, for the second moment, Tonelli's theorem justifies the expansion
\[
E\!\left[
\left(
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_j
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_k
\right)^2
\right]
=
\sum_{j,k,l,m\ge1}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{l m}
E\!\left[
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_j
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_k
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_l
(\mathbb{V}_{\infty})_m
\right].
\]
The same case-by-case classification as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lm_quadratic form} applies. The only nonzero
contributions are
\[
j=k=l=m,\qquad
j=k\neq l=m,\qquad
j=l\neq k=m,\qquad
j=m\neq k=l.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\mathrm{Var}\!\left[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\Pi_n
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\right]
=
(\mu_4-3\sigma_0^4)
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jj}^2
+
\sigma_0^4
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}^2
+
\sigma_0^4
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}(\mathbb{M}_n)_{kj}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}^2
=
\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n'),
\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jk}(\mathbb{M}_n)_{kj}
=
\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n^2),
\]
which gives the desired result.
\end{proof}


\begin{lemma}\label{lem:twfe-master-qf}
Suppose Assumptions~1$'$, 2, 7 and \ref{asp_A2} hold. Let \(\Pi_n\) be either \(\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\) or
\(\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\), and let \(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\) and \(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\) be two nonstochastic
\(n\times\infty\) matrices that are UB. Then
\[
E\Bigl[(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'\Pi_n(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})\Bigr]=
O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\mathrm{Var}\Bigl[(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'\Pi_n(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})\Bigr]
=O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{1}{NT}
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
-
\frac{1}{NT}E\Bigl[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\Bigr]
=
O_p\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),
\]
\[
\frac{1}{NT}
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\widebar{\mathbb{P}}
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
-\frac{1}{NT}
E\Bigl[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\widebar{\mathbb{P}}
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\Bigr]
=O_p\left(\frac{1}{T\sqrt{N}}+\frac{1}{N\sqrt{T}}\right),
\]
where
\(
\frac{1}{NT}
E\Bigl[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\Bigr]
=
O(1)
\)
and
\(
\frac{1}{NT}
E\Bigl[
(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'
\widebar{\mathbb{P}}
(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})
\Bigr]
=
O\!\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)
+
O\!\left(\frac{1}{N}\right).
\)
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~B.3 of Meng and Yang (2026b), both $\widebar{\mathbb{P}}$ and $\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}$ are UB.
Hence \(\Pi_n\) is UB in either case.
The expectation formula follows directly from Lemma~\ref{lem:infinite-qf-homo}:
\[
E\Bigl[(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'\Pi_n(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})\Bigr]
=
\sigma_0^2\,\mathrm{tr}\Bigl(\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'\Bigr).
\]
Moreover,
\begin{align}
\bigl|\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'\bigr)\bigr|
&\le
\mathrm{rank}\bigl(\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'\bigr)\,
\bigl\|\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'\bigr\|_2
\nonumber\\
&\le
\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\,
\Bigl\|
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\Bigr\|_1^{1/2}
\Bigl\|
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\Bigr\|_\infty^{1/2}
=
O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr),\label{eq_rank}
\end{align}
Therefore,
\[
E\Bigl[(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'\Pi_n(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})\Bigr]
=
O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr).
\]

For the variance, let
$\mathbb{M}_n\equiv \mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}.$
By Lemma~\ref{lem:infinite-qf-homo},
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Var}\Bigl[(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'\Pi_n(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})\Bigr]
&=
(\mu_4-3\sigma_0^4)\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jj}^2
+\sigma_0^4\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n')
+\sigma_0^4\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n^2).
\end{align*}
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:infinite-qf-homo},
$$\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n')
=
\mathrm{tr}\!\left(
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}'\Pi_n'
\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\right),\qquad\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n^2)
=
\mathrm{tr}\!\left(
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\Pi_n\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}'
\right).$$ Moreover, $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(\mathbb{M}_n)_{jj}^2
\le
\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n').$
Hence, by the same argument as for the equation (\ref{eq_rank}),
\[
\bigl|\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n\mathbb{M}_n')\bigr|
=
O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr),
\qquad
\bigl|\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{M}_n^2)\bigr|
=
O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr).
\]
Therefore,
\[
\mathrm{Var}\Bigl[(\mathbb{A}_{1,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})'\Pi_n(\mathbb{A}_{2,\infty}\mathbb{V}_{\infty})\Bigr]
=O\bigl(\mathrm{rank}(\Pi_n)\bigr).
\]
Since $\widebar{\mathbb{P}}$ is the orthogonal projection matrix onto the column space of the
two-way fixed effects design matrix $(\mathbb{D},\mathbb{J})$, we have
\(
\mathrm{rank}(\widebar{\mathbb{P}})
=
N+T-1,
\)
where the subtraction of one degree of freedom is due to the normalization on the time fixed effects. Moreover,
\(
\mathrm{rank}(\widebar{\mathbb{Q}})=n-N-T+1=O(NT),
\)
so the stated expectation and stochastic orders follow. The stochastic orders follow from Chebyshev's inequality.
\end{proof}


\begin{lemma}\label{lem:twfe-LV-lln}
Under the Assumptions~1$'$, 2, 7 and \ref{asp_A2}, the following results hold:
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{R}^{\ell}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right), \label{eq:twfe-LV-1} \\
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{R}^{\ell}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{T\sqrt{N}}+\frac{1}{N\sqrt{T}}\right), \label{eq:twfe-LV-2} \\
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right), \label{eq:twfe-LV-3} \\
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{T\sqrt{N}}+\frac{1}{N\sqrt{T}}\right). \label{eq:twfe-LV-4}\\
\frac{1}{NT}
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\mathbb{R}^{\ell}
-
\frac{1}{NT}
E
\left(
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\mathbb{R}^{\ell}
\right)
&=
O_p\left(\frac{1}{N\sqrt{T}}\right), \label{eq:twfe-LV-5} \\
\frac{1}{NT}
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}
-
\frac{1}{NT}
E
\left(
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}
\right)
&=
O_p\left(\frac{1}{N\sqrt{T}}\right). \label{eq:twfe-LV-6}
\end{align}

The expectations satisfy:
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\bigr)&=O(1), &
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\bigr)&=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right), \label{eq:twfe-LV-7} \\
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)&=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right). \label{eq:twfe-LV-8b}
\end{align}
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}
E
\left(
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\mathbb{R}^{\ell}
\right)
=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),\qquad\frac{1}{NT}
E
\left(
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}
\right)
=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right). \label{eq:twfe-LV-10}
\end{align}
Specifically,
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr) &= \frac{\sigma_0^2}{NT}\mathrm{tr}\left[\mathcal{T}^{-1}\sum_{h=1}^{T-1}\sum_{t=T-h}^{T-1}D_{t+1}'B_{t+1}^\ell P_{t}^{(t+h-T)}B_{2,T-h}'D_{T-h}\right] \notag\\
&\quad + \frac{\sigma_0^2}{NT}\mathrm{tr}\left( \mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q} \mathcal{B}_{2\infty} \mathcal{P}_{\infty}^{\ell\prime} \mathbb{B}_1^{\ell\prime}\right) = O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right), \label{eq:twfe-LV-8a}
\end{align}
where $B_{t+1}^\ell \equiv B_{1,t+1}^\ell B_{1,t}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}

We have $\mathbb{L}^\ell = \mathbb{B}_1^\ell \mathcal{P}_\infty^\ell \mathbb{V}_\infty$ and $\mathbb{R}^\ell = \mathbb{B}_2^\ell \mathcal{Q}_\infty^\ell \mathbb{V}_\infty$.
Moreover, we can write $\mathbb{B}_2 \mathbb{V} = \mathcal{B}_{2\infty}\mathbb{V}_\infty$, where $\mathcal{B}_{2\infty}$ is an $n \times \infty$ matrix defined as
$$\mathcal{B}_{2\infty} = \begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{0}_{N_1 \times N_T} & \dots & \mathbf{0}_{N_1 \times N_2} & B_{21} & \mathbf{0}_{N_1 \times N_0} & \dots \\
\mathbf{0}_{N_2 \times N_T} & \dots & B_{22} & \mathbf{0}_{N_2 \times N_1} & \mathbf{0}_{N_2 \times N_0} & \dots \\
\vdots & \iddots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots \\
B_{2T} & \dots & \mathbf{0}_{N_T \times N_2} & \mathbf{0}_{N_T \times N_1} & \mathbf{0}_{N_T \times N_0} & \dots
\end{pmatrix}.$$
Since the matrices $\mathbb{B}_1^\ell \mathcal{P}_\infty^\ell$, $\mathbb{B}_2^\ell \mathcal{Q}_\infty^\ell$, and $\mathcal{B}_{2\infty}$ are all UB according to Assumption~\ref{asp_A2} and Lemma \ref{lem:Pinfty-UB}, Lemma~\ref{lem:twfe-master-qf} can be directly applied to establish \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-1}--\eqref{eq:twfe-LV-4}, and \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-7}--\eqref{eq:twfe-LV-8b}.

To derive the explicit expression \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-8a}, we notice that $\widebar{\mathbb{P}}$ is the projection matrix onto the column space of $[\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{J}]$. We can naturally decompose this into the projection onto $\mathbb{D}$ plus the projection onto the part of $\mathbb{J}$ that is orthogonal to $\mathbb{D}$. Therefore, we have
\(
\widebar{\mathbb{P}} = \mathbb{P} + \mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}.
\)
Then the expectation splits into two terms:
\[
E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr) = E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\mathbb{P}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr) + E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lm_LQV}, the first term yields the double-sum trace formula exactly as in \eqref{eq_ELPV}. For the second term, applying equation \eqref{eq_Einfty}, we have:
\begin{align*}
E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
&= E\bigl( \mathbb{V}_{\infty}^{\prime} \mathcal{P}_{\infty}^{\ell\prime} \mathbb{B}_1^{\ell\prime} \mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q} \mathcal{B}_{2\infty} \mathbb{V}_{\infty} \bigr)\\
&= \sigma_0^2 \, \mathrm{tr}\bigl( \mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q} \mathcal{B}_{2\infty} \mathcal{P}_{\infty}^{\ell\prime} \mathbb{B}_1^{\ell\prime} \bigr).
\end{align*}
Combining these two parts directly yields \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-8a}.


The same argument also applies to the residualized time-effect projection
\(
\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}
\). Since
\(\mathrm{rank}(\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J}
(\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q}\mathbb{J})^{-1}
\mathbb{J}'\mathbb{Q})=T-1\), Lemma~\ref{lem:twfe-master-qf} gives \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-5}--\eqref{eq:twfe-LV-6}, and their expectations satisfy \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-10}.
\end{proof}



\begin{lemma}\label{lem:twfe-ZV-ZZ}
Under Assumptions~1$'$, 2, 3, 4$'$, 5--7 and \ref{asp_A2}, we have
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-1}
\\
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-2}
\\
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-3}
\\
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}-\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}\bigr)
&=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right).
\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-4}
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
&=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\qquad
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-5}
\end{align}
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}\bigr)
&=O(1),
\qquad
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}\bigr)
=O(1).
\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-6}
\end{align}
The results in equations \eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-1}--\eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-4} remain valid when \(\mathbb{Z}\) is replaced by
\(\mathbb{Z}\widetilde{\Gamma}\), where \(\widetilde{\Gamma}=\mathrm{blkdiag}(I_2,\sqrt{T},I_k)\).
Furthermore,
\begin{align}
\sqrt{T}\,\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)'}\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}=O_p(N\sqrt{T}),\qquad
T\,\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)'}\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}=O(NT).\label{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-7}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write
\(
\mathbb{Z}=(\mathbb{Z}_1,\mathbb{Z}_2,\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)},\mathbb{Z}_4),
\)
where \(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}\) is the listing regressor and \(\mathbb{Z}_4\) collects the remaining \(k\) columns.
As in the one-way case, \(\mathbb{B}_1\mathbb{Z}_1,\mathbb{B}_1\mathbb{Z}_2,
\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}_1\), and \(\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}_2\) are all of the form
\(\mathbb{C}+\mathbb{L}^{\ell}\) or \(\mathbb{C}+\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\), while
\(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}\) and the columns of \(\mathbb{Z}_4\) are of the form \(\mathbb{C}\).

We first consider the \(\mathbb{Z}\)-\(\mathbb{V}\) terms. Let
\(\Pi_n\in\{\widebar{\mathbb{Q}},\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\}\). Every element of
\(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\) can be reduced to terms of the form
\[
\mathbb{C}'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V},
\qquad
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}.
\]
Since Lemma~B.3 of Meng and Yang (2026) implies that
\(\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\) and \(\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\) are UB, elements in \(\mathbb{B}_2'\Pi_n\mathbb{C}\)
are still uniformly bounded. Therefore, by equation~\eqref{eq_cv} in
Lemma~\ref{lm_CQL},
\[
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{C}'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}
=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right).
\]
For the second component, Lemma~\ref{lem:twfe-LV-lln} gives
\[
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}
-
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),
\]
with
\[
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}\bigr)
=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right).
\]
Combining these bounds proves equations \eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-1}, \eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-2}, and
\eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-5}.

Next consider the \(\mathbb{Z}\)-\(\mathbb{Z}\) terms. Expanding block by block, every element of
\(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{B}_1'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}\) is a sum of terms of the following types:
\[
\mathbb{C}_1'\Pi_n\mathbb{C}_2,
\qquad
\mathbb{C}'\Pi_n\mathbb{L}^{\ell},
\qquad
\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\Pi_n\mathbb{R}^{\ell}.
\]
The first type is deterministic, and
\(
\mathbb{C}_1'\Pi_n\mathbb{C}_2=O(NT),
\)
because \(\Pi_n\) is UB and \(\mathbb{C}_1,\mathbb{C}_2\) have uniformly bounded elements.

For the second type, \(\Pi_n\mathbb{C}\) is deterministic with uniformly bounded elements. 
Applying equation (\ref{eq_cl}), together with Lemma~\ref{lm_lag}, gives
\[
\frac{1}{NT}\mathbb{C}'\Pi_n\mathbb{L}^{\ell}
=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right).
\]
The expectation is zero. 

The third type is controlled by equations
\eqref{eq:twfe-LV-1}--\eqref{eq:twfe-LV-2} and the expectation bounds in \eqref{eq:twfe-LV-7}. Therefore, equations \eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-3} and \eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-4} hold, and their expectations satisfy equation
\eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-6}.

It remains to verify the statements involving \(\widetilde{\Gamma}\). The matrix \(\widetilde{\Gamma}\)
only multiplies the listing column by \(\sqrt{T}\). Since
\(\Pi_n\in\{\widebar{\mathbb{Q}},\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\}\) is still UB, the same sparse-vector calculations as in
Lemma~\ref{lm_Lambda} give
\[
\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)'}\mathbb{B}_1'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}=O(1),
\qquad
\frac{\sqrt{T}}{NT}\mathbb{C}'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}
=O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\right),
\]
and
\[
\frac{\sqrt{T}}{NT}\mathbb{L}^{\ell\prime}\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}
=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right),
\qquad
\frac{\sqrt{T}}{NT}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)'}\mathbb{B}_1'\Pi_n\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{V}
=O_p\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{NT}}\right).
\]
Together with the bounds already established for the non-listing columns, these equations imply that 
\eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-1}--\eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-4} remain valid after replacing \(\mathbb{Z}\) by
\(\mathbb{Z}\widetilde{\Gamma}\). They also imply
\[
\sqrt{T}\,\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)'}\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}
=O_p\left(N\sqrt{T}\right),
\qquad
T\,\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)'}\mathbb{B}_1'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{B}_2\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}
=O(NT),
\]
which is equation \eqref{eq:twfe-ZV-ZZ-7}.
\end{proof}




\begin{lemma}\label{lem:twfe-bridge}
Under Assumptions~1$'$, 2, 3, 4$'$, 5--7 and \ref{asp_A2}, we have
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\mathbb{Z}'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{Z}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)
-
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)
&=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-bridge-1}
\\
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\mathbb{Z}'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\bigr)
-
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\bigr)
&=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-bridge-2}
\\
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\mathbb{Z}'\mathbb{G}_0'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\bigr)
-
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\bigr)
&=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\label{eq:twfe-bridge-3}
\end{align}
where
\(
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)=O(1),\) \(
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\bigr)=O(1),\) and
\(
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\bigr)=O(1).
\)
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Recall that
\(
\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\circ}=\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}\), \(\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}=\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{Z}+\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\circ},
\)
and similarly
\(
\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{\circ}=\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}\), \(\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}=\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}+\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}}}^{\circ}.
\)
Therefore,
\[
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\mathbb{Z}'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{Z}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)
-
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)
=
\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\mathbb{Z}^{\circ\prime}\widebar{\mathbb{P}}\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}\) has the same structure as in the one-way case, namely
\(
\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}=\bigl(\mathbb{L}^{\ell},\mathbb{R}^{\ell},0_{n\times (k+1)}\bigr),
\)
up to relabeling of the coefficient matrices. Hence, Lemma~\ref{lem:twfe-LV-lln} implies that the right-hand
side is of order \(O(\frac{1}{T})+O(\frac{1}{N})\), which proves \eqref{eq:twfe-bridge-1}. Since $\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\mathbb{Z}'\widebar{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{Z}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)$ is $O(1)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:twfe-ZV-ZZ}, therefore $\frac{1}{NT}E\bigl(\widetilde{\Gamma}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*\prime}\widebar{\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}}^{*}\widetilde{\Gamma}\bigr)=O(1)$.

Equations \eqref{eq:twfe-bridge-2} and \eqref{eq:twfe-bridge-3} are proved in the same way after replacing
\(\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}\) by \(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}^{\circ}\). Under Assumptions~3 and 5, \(\mathbb{G}_0=\mathbb{W}\mathbb{S}_0^{-1}\)
is UB, so Lemmas~\ref{lem:twfe-LV-lln} and
\ref{lem:twfe-ZV-ZZ} continue to apply.
\end{proof}

Since only $O(N)$ observations contain information about $\gamma$, this parameter exhibits a slower convergence rate compared to others. 
Denote $\theta^{(-\gamma)}$ as the vector obtained by removing $\gamma$ from $\theta$, with $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}$ and $\theta^{(-\gamma)}_0$ defined analogously. We will first prove that $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}\overset{p}{\rightarrow}\theta^{(-\gamma)}_0$, then the consistency of $\hat{\gamma}$ follows directly from its explicit expression in terms of $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}$.

Recall that
$$Q_n(\theta)= E[L_n^c(\theta)]=-\frac{n}{2}\ln2\pi-\frac{n}{2}\ln\sigma^2+\ln\left|\mathbb{S}(\rho)\right|-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}E\left[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}'(\zeta)\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)\right].$$
The consistency of $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}$ comes from uniform convergence and identifiable uniqueness, we first show the uniform convergence of $\frac{1}{n}(L_n^c(\theta)-Q_n(\theta))$, and then show the identifiable uniqueness by proving the equicontinuity of $Q_n(\theta)$ and the global identified condition. Our proof follows the idea in Yu et al. (2008).

\textbf{Proof of uniform convergence}

The uniform convergence is specifically defined as $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|\frac{1}{n}\left(L_n^c(\theta)-Q_n(\theta)\right)|\overset{p}{\to}0.$
Denote the true value of each parameter as $\theta_0=(\rho_0,\delta_0',\sigma_0^2)$, $\zeta_0=(\rho_0,\delta_0')$. As


$$\frac{1}{n}\left(L_n^c(\theta)-Q_n(\theta)\right)=\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\left(\frac{1}{n}\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)-\frac{1}{n}E\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)\right),$$
we will first show $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\frac{1}{n}\left|\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)-E\left[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)\right]\right|\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0$.
Since $\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)=\mathbb{Q(Y-\rho WY-Z\delta})$, substituting $\mathbb{Y}$ for $\mathbb{Y}=\rho_0\mathbb{W}\mathbb{Y}+\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V}$, we have $\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)=\mathbb{Q[V-(}\rho-\rho_0)\mathbb{WY-Z}(\delta-\delta_0)]$. Therefore
\begin{align}
\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)=&\mathbb{V'QV}+(\rho-\rho_0)^2\mathbb{(WY)'QWY}+(\delta-\delta_0)'\mathbb{Z'QZ}(\delta-\delta_0)-\nonumber\\
&2(\rho-\rho_0)\mathbb{V'QWY}-2\mathbb{V'QZ}(\delta-\delta_0)+2(\rho-\rho_0)\mathbb{(WY)'QZ}(\delta-\delta_0).\label{eq_V'V}
\end{align}
Since $\mathbb{WY}=\mathbb{G}_0(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V})$, $\mathbb{V'QWY}=\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V}$, $\mathbb{(WY)'QZ}=(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QZ}+(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)'\mathbb{QZ}+(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V)'QZ}$, and
\begin{align}
\mathbb{(WY)'QWY}=&(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V})'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}+\nonumber\\
&2(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+2(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}+2(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}.\label{eq_WYQWY}
\end{align}
Since $\mathbb{G}_0=\mathbb{WS}^{-1}_0=\mathrm{blkdiag}(W_1S_1^{-1},W_2S_2^{-1},\cdots,W_TS_T^{-1})$, where $W_tS_t^{-1}$ is UB uniformly for $t$ and $\|\sup_t \mathrm{abs}(W_tS_t^{-1})\|_\infty<\infty$ is ensured by Assumption 5 and Lemma \ref{lm33}, it follows from Lemma \ref{lm15} that
\begin{align*}
&\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{V'QV}-\frac{1}{n}E[\mathbb{V'QV}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{n}E[\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,\\
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V})'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V})'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{Z'QZ}-\frac{1}{n}E[\mathbb{Z'QZ}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,\\
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QZ}-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QZ}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,\\
&\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{V'QZ}-\frac{1}{n}E[\mathbb{V'QZ}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0-\frac{1}{n}E[\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,\\
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V)'QZ}-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{V)'QZ}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0.
\end{align*}
Additionally, according to Lemma \ref{lm_CQL}, 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{V'Q}\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{V}\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
\\
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)'\mathbb{QZ}-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)'\mathbb{QZ}]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0,
&\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0-\frac{1}{n}E[(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0)'\mathbb{QG}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0]\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0.
\end{align*}
Therefore, all polynomial coefficients in $\frac{1}{n}\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)$ will converge to their expected values. 
Since $\rho$ and $\delta$ are bounded in $\Theta$, it follows that $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\frac{1}{n}|\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)-E[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)]|\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0$. Since $\sigma^2$ is bounded away from zero, we therefore have $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\frac{1}{n}|L_n^c(\theta)-Q_n(\theta)|\stackrel{p}{\rightarrow}0$.

\textbf{Proof of equicontinuity}

Next we prove that $\frac{1}{n}Q_n(\theta)$ is uniformly equicontinuous for $\theta\in\Theta$, which is specifically defined as for any $\epsilon>0$, there exists $\eta>0$ and $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$, such that whenever $d(\theta,\bar{\theta})<\eta$ and $n>n_0$, we have 
$$\left|\frac{1}{n}\left(Q_n(\theta)-Q_n(\bar{\theta})\right)\right|<\epsilon.$$
Since 
$$\frac{1}{n}Q_n(\theta)=-\frac{1}{2}\ln2\pi-\frac{1}{2}\ln\sigma^2+\frac{1}{n}\ln|\mathbb{S}(\rho)|-\frac{1}{2n\sigma^2}E\left[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}'(\zeta)\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)\right],$$
where $E[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}'(\zeta)\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)]=\mathbb{(\mathbb{S(\rho)}Y-Z\delta)'Q(\mathbb{S(\rho)}Y-Z\delta})$, substitute $\mathbb{Y}$ for $\mathbb{Y=S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V})$, then
\begin{align}
E[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)]=&E\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V})-\mathbb{Z\delta}\right)'\mathbb{Q}\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V})-\mathbb{Z\delta}\right)\right]\nonumber\\
=&E\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)-\mathbb{Z\delta}\right)'\mathbb{Q}\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)-\mathbb{Z\delta}\right)\right]\nonumber\\
&+E\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\mathbb{V}\right)'\mathbb{QS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\mathbb{V}\right]
+2E\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)-\mathbb{Z\delta}\right)'\mathbb{QS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\mathbb{V}\right],\label{eq_EVTV}
\end{align}
where $E\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\mathbb{V}\right)'\mathbb{QS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\mathbb{V}\right]=\sigma^2_0\mathrm{tr}\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right)'\mathbb{QS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right]$,
and $$E\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)-\mathbb{Z\delta}\right)'\mathbb{QS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\mathbb{V}\right]=O(N)$$
by Lemma \ref{lm15}.

Denote $\sigma^2_n\equiv\frac{\sigma^2_0}{n}\mathrm{tr}[(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1})'\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}]$. Since
\begin{align*}
\frac{\sigma^2_0}{n}\mathrm{tr}\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right)'\mathbb{PS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right]&=\frac{\sigma^2_0}{n}\mathrm{tr}\left[\mathbb{D}\mathcal{T}^{-1}\mathbb{D'S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right)'\right]\\
&\leq\frac{\sigma^2_0}{c_TnT}\mathrm{tr}\left[\mathrm{abs}\left(\mathbb{D'S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right)'\mathbb{D}\right)\right]=O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right),
\end{align*}
where the inequality holds because $T_i>c_TT$ by Assumption 1 and the matrix inside the trace operation is UB. Thus, $\frac{\sigma^2_0}{n}\mathrm{tr}\left[\left(\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right)'\mathbb{QS(\rho)S}_0^{-1}\right]=\sigma^2_n+O\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)$. Further substitute $\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}$ for $\mathbb{S(\rho)S}_0^{-1}=I_n+(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0$, then we have
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{n}E[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)]=&\frac{1}{n}E\left\{\left[(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)+\mathbb{Z}(\delta_0-\delta)\right]'\mathbb{Q}\left[(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)+\mathbb{Z}(\delta_0-\delta)\right]\right\}\nonumber\\
&+\sigma^2_n+o(1),\label{EVV}
\end{align}
where the first term is equal to $(\rho-\rho_0,\delta'-\delta_0')E[\mathcal{H}](\rho-\rho_0,\delta'-\delta_0')'$, and $\mathcal{H}\equiv\frac{1}{n}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0,\mathbb{Z})'\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0,\mathbb{Z})$.
Therefore, the uniform equicontinuity of $\frac{1}{n}Q_n(\theta)$ is sufficient to show the following is uniformly equicontinuous: (i) $-\frac{1}{2}\ln\sigma^2$; (ii) $\frac{1}{n}\ln|\mathbb{S(\rho)}|$;
(iii) $(\rho-\rho_0,\delta'-\delta_0')E[\mathcal{H}](\rho-\rho_0,\delta'-\delta_0')'$; (iv) $\sigma^2_n$.

Since $\sigma^2$ is bounded away from zero, (i) is obviously uniformly equicontinuous.
For (ii), $\frac{1}{n}(\ln|\mathbb{S(\rho}_1)|-\ln|\mathbb{S(\rho}_2)|)=(\rho_1-\rho_2)\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{WS}^{-1}(\Bar{\rho}))$, where $\Bar{\rho}$ lies between $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$. According to equation (\ref{eq_Grho}), 
$\sup_{N,T}\|\mathbb{W}\mathbb{S}^{-1}(\Bar{\rho})\|_{\infty}<\infty$, so $\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{WS}^{-1}(\Bar{\rho}))$ is bounded, which means that (ii) is uniformly equicontinuous.
(iii) is uniformly equicontinuous because the parameter space $(\rho,\delta)$ is bounded and $E[\mathcal{H}]$ is $O(1)$. 
For (iv), 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{\sigma^2_0}{n}\{\mathrm{tr}[(\mathbb{S(\rho}_1)\mathbb{S}_0^{-1})'\mathbb{QS(\rho}_1)\mathbb{S}_0^{-1}]-\mathrm{tr}[(\mathbb{S(\rho}_2)\mathbb{S}_0^{-1})'\mathbb{QS(\rho}_2)\mathbb{S}_0^{-1}]\}\\
=&\frac{\sigma^2_0}{n}\{(\rho_0-\rho_1)^2\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{G}_0'\mathbb{QG}_0)+2(\rho_0-\rho_1)\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Q})-(\rho_0-\rho_2)^2\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{G}_0'\mathbb{QG}_0)-2(\rho_0-\rho_2)\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Q})\}\\
=&2(\rho_2-\rho_1)\sigma^2_0\frac{\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Q})}{n}+(2\rho_0-\rho_1-\rho_2)(\rho_2-\rho_1)\sigma^2_0\frac{\mathrm{tr}(\mathbb{G}_0'\mathbb{QG}_0)}{n}.
\end{align*}
Since $\mathbb{G}_0$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ are UB, similarly (iv) is uniformly equicontinuous.

\textbf{Proof of global identification condition}

Then we prove that $\theta_0$, except $\gamma_0$, is identified, which is specifically defined as $\forall\theta^{(-\gamma)}\neq\theta^{(-\gamma)}_0$,
$$\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}[Q_{n}(\theta)-Q_{n}(\theta_{0})]<0.$$ 
Note that
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{n}\left(Q_n(\theta)-Q_n(\theta_0)\right)=-\frac{1}{2}\left(\ln\sigma^2-\ln\sigma^2_0\right)+\frac{1}{n}\left(\ln|\mathbb{S}(\rho)|-\ln|\mathbb{S}_0|\right)-\frac{1}{2n\sigma^2}E\left[\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)'\widetilde{\mathbb{V}}(\zeta)\right]+\frac{c_{u}T-1}{2c_{u}T},\label{Q-Q0}
\end{align}
where $c_u\equiv\frac{n}{NT}$. According to equation (\ref{EVV}), we can decompose equation (\ref{Q-Q0}) into
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{n}\left(Q_n(\theta)-Q_n(\theta_0)\right)=L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}L_2(\rho,\delta)+o(1),
\end{align*}
where $L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)\equiv-\frac{1}{2}\left(\ln\sigma^2-\ln\sigma^2_0\right)+\frac{1}{n}\left(\ln|\mathbb{S}(\rho)|-\ln|\mathbb{S}_0|\right)-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}(\sigma^2_n-\sigma^2)$ and $L_2(\rho,\delta)\equiv\frac{1}{n}E\{[(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)+\mathbb{Z}(\delta_0-\delta)]'\mathbb{Q}[(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0(\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)+\mathbb{Z}(\delta_0-\delta)]\}$.









For a spatial autoregressive model 
$\mathbb{Y}=\rho_0\mathbb{WY+V}$ with $v_{it}\sim \mathrm{N}(0,\sigma_0^2)$, the information inequality of this model ensures that
$$-\frac{1}{2}\left(\ln\sigma^2-\ln\sigma^2_0\right)+\frac{1}{n}\left(\ln|\mathbb{S}(\rho)|-\ln|\mathbb{S}_0|\right)-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}(\sigma^2_n-\sigma^2)\leq0.$$
Note that left-hand side of the above equation is precisely $L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)$.

Denote $\delta^{(-\gamma)}$ as the vector obtained by removing $\gamma$ from $\delta$, with $\hat{\delta}^{(-\gamma)}$ and $\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0$ defined analogously. By decomposing $\mathbb{Z}\delta$ into $\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)}\delta^{(-\gamma)}+ \mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}\gamma$, $L_2(\rho,\delta)$ can be viewed as a quadratic function of $\rho$, $\delta^{(-\gamma)}$ and $\gamma$, i.e.,
\begin{align*}
L_2(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)},\gamma)=&\left(\rho-\rho_0,\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}-\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}_0\right)E\left[\mathcal{H}^{(-\gamma)}\right]\left(\rho-\rho_0,\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}-\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}_0\right)'+\\
&+\frac{2}{n}\left[(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0(E\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)+E\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)}(\delta^{(-\gamma)}-\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0)\right]'\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\gamma+\frac{1}{n}\gamma'\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\gamma,
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal{H}^{(-\gamma)}=\frac{1}{n}'(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0,\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)})'\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{G}_0\mathbb{D}\alpha_0,\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)})$, and $\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}=\left((D_1F_1\iota_N)',\cdots,(D_TF_T\iota_N)'\right)'$ is a sparse binary vector with at most $N$ nonzero elements, as we can only observe at most $N$ listed nodes. Therefore, $$\frac{2}{n}\left[(\rho_0-\rho)\mathbb{G}_0(E\mathbb{Z}\delta_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0)+E\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)}(\delta^{(-\gamma)}-\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0)\right]'\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\gamma+\frac{1}{n}\gamma'\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\gamma=o(1),$$
because elements in $E\mathbb{Z}$ and $E\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)}$ are uniformly bounded and $\mathbb{G}_0$ is UB. Thus
$$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} L_2(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)},\gamma)=\left(\rho-\rho_0,\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}-\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}_0\right)E\left[\mathcal{H}^{(-\gamma)}\right]\left(\rho-\rho_0,\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}-\delta^{(-\gamma)\prime}_0\right)'\geq0,$$
because $\mathcal{H}^{(-\gamma)}$ is a quadratic form.

Below we will show that $(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)})$ is globally identified by using either Assumption 8 (i) or Assumption 8 (ii).
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Using Assumption 8 (i))
According to Assumption 8 (i), we have $\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} L_2(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)},\gamma)>0$ whenever $(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)})\neq(\rho_0,\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0)$. Combined with $L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)\leq0$, it implies that $(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)})$ is globally identified.
\item (Using Assumption 8 (ii)) Since $\sigma^2_n$ is uniquely maximizer of $L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)$ over $\sigma^2$, the information inequality of the SAR model imples that $L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)\leq L_1(\rho,\sigma^2_n)\leq0$. Moreover, $L_1(\rho,\sigma^2_n)=0$ if and only if the pdf $f(\mathbb{Y}|\rho,\sigma^2_n)= f(\mathbb{Y}|\rho_0,\sigma^2_0)$, where
$$f(\mathbb{Y}|\rho,\sigma^2_n)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^\frac{n}{2}\left|\sigma_n^2\mathbb{S}(\rho)^{-1}\mathbb{S}(\rho)^{-1\prime}\right|^{\frac{1}{2}}}\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2\sigma_n^2}\mathbb{Y'S}(\rho)'\mathbb{S}(\rho)\mathbb{Y}\right].$$
If Assumption 8 (ii) holds, $f(\mathbb{Y}|\rho,\sigma^2_n)\neq f(\mathbb{Y}|\rho_0,\sigma^2_0)$ for $\rho\neq\rho_0$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Then $\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}L_1(\rho,\sigma^2)<0$ whenever $\rho\neq\rho_0$. Combined with $\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} L_2(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)},\gamma)\geq0$, $\rho_0$ is globally identified. Then $\delta^{(-\gamma)}$ will also be identified because, $$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} L_2(\rho_0,\delta^{(-\gamma)},\gamma)=\left(\delta^{(-\gamma)}-\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0\right)'\left[\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}E\left(\mathbb{Z}^{(-\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(-\gamma)}\right)\right]\left(\delta^{(-\gamma)}-\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0\right)>0$$
whenever $\delta^{(-\gamma)}\neq\delta^{(-\gamma)}_0$ by Assumption 4.
\end{enumerate}






Once $(\rho,\delta^{(-\gamma)})$ is globally identified, $\sigma^2$ is also globally identified because $\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}L_1(\rho_0,\sigma^2)=\frac{1}{2}(\ln\frac{\sigma_0^2}{\sigma^2}-\frac{\sigma_0^2}{\sigma^2}+1)\leq0$ and the equality holds if and only if $\sigma^2=\sigma^2_0$, because $\ln x-x+1\leq0$ and the equality holds only when $x=1$.
Therefore, $\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\left(Q_n(\theta)-Q_n(\theta_0)\right)<0$ for any $\theta^{(-\gamma)}\neq\theta^{(-\gamma)}_0$, which means $\theta^{(-\gamma)}$ is globally identified.






Since $\Theta$ is compact and $Q_n(\theta)$ is uniformly equicontinuous, combined with uniformly convergence and global identification of $\theta^{(-\gamma)}$, we can prove the consistency of $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}$. Given $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}$, $L_n^c(\theta)$ is maximized at 
\begin{align*}
\hat{\gamma}&=\left(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\right)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{Q\left(S(\hat{\rho})Y-Z^{(-\gamma)}\hat{\delta}^{(-\gamma)}\right)}\\
&=\left(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\right)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{Q}\left(\mathbb{S(\hat{\rho})S}_0^{-1}\left(\mathbb{Z^{(-\gamma)}}\delta_0^{(-\gamma)}+\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}\gamma_0+\mathbb{D}\alpha_0+\mathbb{V}\right)-\mathbb{Z^{(-\gamma)}\hat{\delta}^{(-\gamma)}}\right).
\end{align*}
Since $\hat{\theta}^{(-\gamma)}\overset{p}{\rightarrow}\theta_0^{(-\gamma)}$, 
$
\hat{\gamma}=\gamma_0+(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)})^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QV}+o_p(1)$.
Additionally,
$(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)})^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QV}=o_p(1)$ because $E[(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)})^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QV}]=0$ and
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Var}\left[\left(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\right)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QV}\right]&=\sigma_0^2\left(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{QZ}^{(\gamma)}\right)^{-1}=\sigma_0^2\left(\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)\prime}\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}-\mathbb{Z^{(\gamma)\prime}D}\mathcal{T}^{-1}\mathbb{D'Z}^{(\gamma)}\right)^{-1}\\
&\leq\sigma_0^2\left[(1-c_N)N-\frac{N}{c_TT}\right]^{-1}=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\end{align*}
where the inequality holds because $\mathbb{Z}^{(\gamma)}$ is a binary vector with at least $(1-c_N)N$ nonzero elements and $T_i\geq c_TT$ by Assumption 1.
Therefore, $\hat{\gamma}\overset{p}{\rightarrow}\gamma_0$, so $\hat{\theta}\overset{p}{\rightarrow}\theta_0$.
